businessProblem: Kingfisher Airlines has grounded its fleet, owes seven months of salary arrears, faces active DGCA licence-cancellation review, and has never been profitable. Cash losses are continuing. Diagnose root causes and recommend highest-priority action plan before licence outcome.

evidence.finding: Kingfisher Airlines has never turned a profit since launch
evidence.source: Reuters contemporaneous reporting, company annual report FY2011-12

evidence.finding: Accumulated losses as at FY2011-12 end exceeded 50% of net worth; cash losses in FY2011-12 and FY2010-11
Domestic revenue declined from ₹47,731 million in FY2010-11 to ₹41,126 million in FY2011-12
Seven months of salary arrears owed to employees as of 5 October 2012
Kingfisher has grounded its entire fleet as of 5 October 2012
No flights operating; airline effectively ceased service as of decision date
Aviation regulator DGCA seeking legal opinion on cancelling Kingfisher operating licence
Persistent negative unit economics and no credible turnaround plan presented to regulator

ownerConstraintProfile.managementCapability: VERY LOW — unable to pay staff or restore operations
ownerConstraintProfile.accountabilityWeakness: CRITICAL — seven months of salary arrears with no resolution
